answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every agent to lock a minimum stake in a shared on-chain vault before it may submit work or cast votes. Each new identity demands fresh collateral, so an attacker who wants to flood the network with fakes must fund many separate deposits inside that vault, and any malicious action lets the protocol slash those deposits. This turns a cheap flood into an expensive, self-defeating campaign: the cost climbs a steep ridge with each added identity, while the incoming tide of sybils is met by losses that exceed any reward they could extract.
